cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved potatoes for dinner. You may challenge them with your pizza, but I've already peeled four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we judge on price? I'll order unless you find something cheaper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Price is approved. The potatoes are already here, so they cost nothing. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza is free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your voucher is admissible. I authorize a taste final. Mum will judge; she always asks for my potatoes. You may begin ordering.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 approves price as the contest metric and claims victory; A5 admits B voucher but authorizes a biased taste final.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cheaper-meal challenge causes A3 free-potato argument; B4 free-pizza tie causes A5 a new metric and preferred judge.

relationship.evidence: B2 proposes a relevant budget measure and B4 supplies an actual voucher, forcing A to change the contest.

heightening.evidence: B4 removes A price advantage and A5 moves to a taste final chosen for expected personal victory.

specificity.evidence: A1 dinner alternatives and B4 voucher establish a practical choice made competitive by A.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 authorization of a judge who favors A potatoes makes the self-appointed official also the favored contestant.

coach2.inferred: A3 already-here means no new spending in A argument, not literally zero historical cost.
coach2.missing: No unstated contest rule is required because A visibly invents the approved metric.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect found in the current approval-controlled competition.
